name: Li Andersson - Annexe I, § 11 - Am 22
title: REPORT on the proposal for a Council decision on guidelines for the employment policies of the Member States
part_text: As a complement to fully tapping the potential of the Union domestic workforce, Member States should attract talent and skills from outside the Union via legal migration pathways, while guaranteeing fair recruitment, equal treatment, labour and social rights, access to collective bargaining and trade union representation, and effective protection against exploitation, discrimination and abusive recruitment practices. Member States should ensure that procedures to recognise qualifications of third-country nationals in the context of legal migration procedures are simple, efficient and facilitate fast access to regulated professions. Member States should further engage in Talent Partnerships to enhance legal migration pathways by launching new mobility schemes and provide for an effective integration policy for workers and their families, encompassing education and training, employment, social protection, health and housing. Labour migration instruments should be governed with equal representation of trade unions and employers. Third-country and mobile workers should receive accessible complaint tools, legal redress and trade-union contact information. Member States should similarly ensure that labour migration does not result in a deterioration of existing working conditions for domestic workers.
